scene.note: The React order screen runs on your store: every part reads only what it shows, and React draws a part again only when that changed.

steps.note: The header calls useStore with a selector for the count. useStore hands React the store's subscribe, and a function that reads the count.
After every change of the store, React reads the count again.
A new count, and React draws the header again, showing it. When the header leaves the page, its subscription stops.
A customer chooses another paper, and the store tells React.
React reads the header's part. The count is the same number as before.
The same part, so React skips the draw. For a part made new on every read, isEqual says it is the same, and useStore hands back the part from before.
A customer removes a line with the basket's button, which calls the store's remove action.
Each part reads only what it shows, from the one store, with useStore.
The header's count and the total change together, worked out from the same basket.
